entities.name: Shams Tabrizi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shams Tabrīzī (1185–1248) was a Persian dervish and poet, best known for his companionship with Rumi.

Born in Tabriz, Persia (modern-day Iran), Tabrīzī's life was deeply intertwined with the spiritual and artistic movements of the time.

In the 1220s, Tabrīzī began his spiritual journey under the guidance of the renowned Sufi master, Shams of Tabriz.

This mentorship had a profound impact on Rumi, who was deeply influenced by Tabrīzī's teachings and poetry, leading to the famous 'Meeting of the Eyes' in Konya, Anatolia (modern-day Turkey), which marked the beginning of their long and iconic friendship.

Tabrīzī's spiritual and literary output continued to flourish during his time with Rumi, producing works such as the 'Masnavi-e Ma'navi', a seminal work of Sufi poetry.

Tabrīzī's death in 1248 marked the end of an era, leaving behind a legacy that would have a lasting impact on the development of Sufi thought and art in the Middle East and beyond.

In the centuries that followed, Tabrīzī's poetry and teachings continued to inspire generations of Sufi mystics and artists, cementing his place as one of the most influential figures in Persian Sufism.

The influence of Tabrīzī can also be seen in the works of other notable Sufi poets and thinkers, such as Hafiz and Ibn Arabi, further solidifying his position as a central figure in the history of Sufism.

Today, Tabrīzī's poetry and legacy continue to be celebrated and studied around the world, a testament to the enduring power of his spiritual and artistic vision.
